facts.label: Read replicas per source (MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL)
facts.note: Oracle and SQL Server allow 5; Aurora allows 15 per cluster.

facts.label: Maximum storage (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB)
facts.note: 64 TiB. SQL Server 16 TiB on most storage types. Aurora up to 256 TiB on recent versions.

facts.label: Backup retention
facts.note: 7 days in the console, 1 day by API.

facts.label: DB instances per Region
facts.note: Shared with Aurora, Neptune and DocumentDB.

facts.label: Multi-AZ failover time (typical)
facts.note: Typical, not guaranteed. Multi-AZ DB clusters: under 35 s.

facts.label: Change the instance class (Single-AZ)
facts.note: The database is unavailable while the new class is applied; AWS does not give a duration.
facts.mitigation: Apply in the maintenance window, or use Multi-AZ or a blue/green deployment first.

facts.label: Change the instance class (Multi-AZ)
facts.note: Connections drop during the failover to the resized standby; typical failover is 60–120 s, longer with large transactions.
facts.mitigation: Apply in the maintenance window; client retries and a DNS TTL of 60 s or less; RDS Proxy keeps connections.

facts.label: Change the instance class (Multi-AZ DB cluster)
facts.note: Downtime whether applied now or in the window; failover typically under 35 s.

facts.label: Add a read replica
facts.note: On a Single-AZ source the snapshot pauses I/O for about a second (Multi-AZ: none, the standby is used).
facts.mitigation: Use a Multi-AZ source; add replicas at low traffic.

facts.label: Increase storage
facts.note: No outage; storage optimisation can take hours, and the next storage change waits until it finishes.
facts.mitigation: Storage autoscaling; grow by at least 10 %.

facts.label: Apply immediately
facts.note: Without Apply immediately the change waits for the maintenance window; with it, every pending change applies now.
facts.mitigation: Review pending modifications before applying now.
